inbox.title: How does the Inbox work?
inbox.description: The Inbox brings every WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, Telegram and SMS conversation into a single chat-style view in real time. Use it to reply yourself, let the AI handle it, or take over when a customer needs a human (handoff).
tips: Filter by 'Unassigned' or 'Mine' to focus; conversations handed to a human show an orange badge.
When you pick up a handoff, you'll see an AI-generated summary of the conversation at the top.
Open the right-hand panel to view and edit the contact's data without leaving the chat.
Use macros and canned responses to reply to common cases in one click (set them up in Settings → Macros).
If a conversation waits more than 5 minutes, it's automatically escalated to a supervisor.

contacts.title: How to manage your contacts?
contacts.description: The CRM brings together everyone who has messaged your business on any channel, unified into a single profile. Use it to store their information, classify them by stage or tags, and follow up without losing the history.
tips: Create a lead manually with the '+ Contact' button (phone is required), or let them be created automatically when a customer writes in.
Click a contact to open its 360° detail: timeline, conversations, score and custom fields.
Use 'Advanced filters' to segment by score, tags or date (e.g. leads with score > 80 from this week).
Select several with the checkboxes for bulk actions: change stage, add a tag, or archive.
The score is computed from 5 factors; click the number to see the breakdown.

pipeline.title: How does the sales pipeline work?
pipeline.description: The pipeline is a Kanban board where each card is a sales opportunity and each column is a stage of your process (e.g. New → Contacted → Qualified → Won). It lets you see at a glance where every deal stands and decide who to follow up with first.
tips: Drag a card between columns to change its stage; for example, move a lead from 'Contacted' to 'Qualified' once they confirm interest.
Dropping a card into a terminal stage (Won/Lost) can require approval; pending ones show a yellow badge.
Each stage's value and probability feed the sales forecast shown above the board.
Customize stage names, colors and probabilities in Settings → Tools → Pipeline stages.
Use the search and filters to focus on an agent, a channel, or deals with an SLA at risk.

appointments.title: How do I manage appointments and availability?
appointments.description: The appointments section is a full calendar where you view, create, and edit your customers' bookings, set up services with duration and price, and connect Google Calendar or Microsoft for two-way sync. The AI agent uses this configuration to schedule automatically.
tips: Before activating the agent to schedule, go to the 'Config' tab and save your availability schedule; without that step, the bot will reply that no time slots are available.
In the 'Services' tab, create each service with its duration, price, and rest buffer; the agent only offers services that are active.
Click any cell in the calendar to create a manual appointment; you can also drag an existing appointment to reschedule it.
Connect Google Calendar or Microsoft in 'Config' so that external appointments automatically block those slots and you avoid double bookings.
24h and 1h reminders are sent automatically; enable or disable them with the 'Reminders' toggles in the 'Config' tab.

properties.title: How do I manage my rental properties?
properties.description: The Properties section is your vacation rental catalog: register each unit with photos, rooms, bathrooms, capacity, nightly price, cleaning fee, and amenities. Use it so the AI agent has everything it needs to quote and book automatically with your clients.
tips: Click 'New property' to register a unit; the name and nightly price are the minimum required for the agent to quote it.
Check the actual amenities for each unit (WiFi, Pool, Pet friendly, etc.) — the agent mentions them when a client asks what is included.
Set the correct currency (COP, USD, MXN, etc.) so prices are shown in the local context your clients expect.
Set 'Minimum nights' to avoid unprofitable single-night bookings; for example, enter 2 if your minimum stay is two nights.
Click on a property card to open its detail page, upload photos, and manage the availability calendar.

broadcast.title: How do I create and send a broadcast campaign?
broadcast.description: Broadcast lets you send bulk messages to your contacts via WhatsApp or Email in one shot, with real-time delivery and read tracking. Use it for promotions, important announcements, or re-engaging inactive customers.
tips: Click '+ Create' and choose the channel (WhatsApp or Email); for WhatsApp, enter the exact name of your Meta-approved template in the 'Template' field.
Under 'Audience', pick 'All contacts' to reach your entire base, or select a saved 'Segment' to target a specific group (e.g., qualified leads from this month).
Toggle 'A/B Test' (available on Pro+ plans) to test two message versions and let the platform identify the winner based on read rate.
Leave the date field empty to save as a draft and send manually with 'Send now', or schedule an exact date and time for automatic delivery.
Once sent, click the campaign to see metrics: recipients, delivered (green), and read (blue) on the progress bar.

automation.title: How do I create and manage automations?
automation.description: Automations are 'if X happens, then do Y' rules that run on their own in the background. Use them to send follow-ups, change lead stages, assign agents, or add tags without manual intervention.
tips: Create a rule with the '+ New rule' button and choose a trigger: for example, 'Lead captured' to automatically welcome every new prospect.
Add conditions in step 2 of the wizard to filter: for example, only activate the rule if the channel is 'WhatsApp' and the score is above 60.
In step 3, define chained actions: first 'Change stage' to 'Qualified' and then 'Send template' as a welcome message, all in a single rule.
Use the activity icon (chart) on each card to view the execution history and confirm the rule is firing correctly.
Enable or disable a rule with the toggle without deleting it — ideal for pausing temporary campaigns without losing your configuration.

agent.title: How do I manage my AI Agents?
agent.description: AI agents are the virtual assistants that automatically reply to your customers on WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, or Telegram. Here you create, duplicate, and organize all your agents, and see which channels each one is assigned to.
tips: Click 'New agent' to pick a template for your industry (sales, support, scheduling, etc.) and give it a name before creating it.
Use the three-dot menu on each card to 'Save as template' and reuse the setup for future agents.
If you see the red 'Channels without agent' banner, open that agent and assign the channel before messages go unanswered.
The star icon in the menu lets you set an agent as 'Default'; this one replies when no channel has a specific assignment.
Duplicate an existing agent with the copy icon to create variations (e.g., one in Spanish and one in English) without starting from scratch.

knowledge.title: How do I manage the Knowledge Base?
knowledge.description: The Knowledge Base is your AI agent's memory: upload documents, add URLs to crawl automatically, create FAQs, and organize everything into categories. The more complete and up to date it is, the more accurate the agent's answers will be for your customers.
tips: Use the 'Bulk upload' button to load multiple files (PDF, Word, TXT) at once and assign them a category in the same step.
For web pages that change frequently (prices, menus, catalogs), use 'Add URL' and enable automatic re-crawl so the content stays up to date on its own.
In the 'Quality' tab you'll see a score from 0 to 100 for each document — prioritize the ones with low scores to rewrite or enrich them with more detail.
In the 'Analytics' tab review the 'Unanswered Queries': these are real questions the agent couldn't handle; create an article directly from that list by clicking the '+' icon.
Use the 'Gaps' tab together with 'AI Suggestions' to let the system automatically detect missing topics in your base and propose titles and outlines for new articles.

analyticsV2.title: How do I read the Advanced Analytics?
analyticsV2.description: Advanced analytics brings together conversation performance, AI, campaigns, automations, and CSAT in one place, with real-time data and date filters. Use them to make data-driven decisions and catch problems before they escalate.
tips: The real-time panel (top) refreshes every 30 seconds; if 'Queue depth' rises, there are messages waiting that need attention.
Change the period with the 'DateRangePicker' and then click 'Export CSV' to download the data and work on it in Excel.
In the 'IA & Bot' tab, check the 'AI Resolution Rate': if it drops below 70%, review the agent rules or enrich the knowledge base.
The 'Anomalies' tab alerts you automatically when a metric strays from its historical average (more than 2σ), saving you manual monitoring.
Use the 'Broadcast' tab to see your campaign funnel (total → sent → delivered → read) and optimize low-read-rate templates.

channels.title: How do I connect and manage channels?
channels.description: Channels is the hub where you connect each messaging network (WhatsApp, Instagram DM, Facebook Messenger, Telegram, and Email) so your AI agent can receive and reply from everywhere. Each card shows whether the channel is 'Connected' or 'Disconnected' and takes you to its individual settings.
tips: Click 'Configure' on the WhatsApp card to start Meta's Embedded Signup; you'll need a WhatsApp Business account and a Facebook page.
For Instagram DM, the account must be a professional account linked to a Facebook page; the process uses OAuth and takes under 2 minutes.
Connecting Messenger requires logging in with Facebook (FB SDK) and selecting your business page to get the messaging token.
Telegram only needs a Bot Token: create a bot with @BotFather, copy the token, and paste it in the channel settings.
A connected channel shows the green 'Connected' badge; if you see the red 'Disconnected' badge, open the card to reconnect and assign an AI agent.

users.title: How do I manage the team and invitations?
users.description: The Users section shows all team members with their role, skills, status, and company, and lets you invite new people by email. Use it to control who has access, what each person can do, and which conversations get routed to each agent.
tips: Click 'Invite user', enter the email, and choose a role (Agent, Supervisor, or Admin); the person will receive an email with a secure link to set their password.
Under the 'Invitations' tab you can see the status of each invitation (pending, accepted, expired, or revoked); if one expired, resend it with the 'Resend' button.
Add skill tags to agents — for example 'sales', 'support', or 'technical' — so the system automatically routes messages to the most suitable agent.
Use the search bar and role filter to quickly find a team member; filter by Agent, Supervisor, or Admin.
Click 'Edit' to update a user's name, job title, phone, role, or active/inactive status; deactivating someone prevents them from logging in until you reactivate them.

settings.title: What can I configure in this section?
settings.description: Settings is the central panel where you adjust everything that controls platform behavior: your profile and security, company information, operational tools, external integrations, and advanced AI parameters. Use it whenever you need to change how the system works or add new connections.
tips: Under 'Account' you can change your password, enable 2FA, and set your notification schedule so you are not interrupted outside your shift.
Under 'Company' you will find 'Business Hours': configure your actual working days and times so the AI agent knows when human support is available.
Under 'Operations' customize the pipeline stages and the lead scoring weights to match your own sales process.
Under 'Communication' create macros with frequent replies so your human agents can respond faster from the Inbox.
Under 'Integrations' connect outbound webhooks, your Web Chat, or a vertical integration (Toast, Mindbody, Cliniko) to sync data with your external tools.

tenants.title: How do I manage platform tenants?
tenants.description: The Tenants section is the exclusive super admin panel where you can view, create, and manage all companies (tenants) registered on Parallly. Use it to monitor each account's status, manage billing and subscriptions, review onboarding progress, and perform administrative actions such as suspending or impersonating a tenant.
tips: Use the 'Overview' tab to see the full tenant table with plan, subscription status, connected channels, and user count; click 'Impersonate' to enter the platform as that tenant.
The 'Onboarding' tab shows which accounts have not completed initial setup (no connected channel or no configured agent) so you can reach out to them.
Under 'Offboarding' manage tenants in the cancellation process: you can suspend them with a reason or reactivate them if the client changes their mind.
The 'Billing' tab consolidates MRR, ARR, and payment status for each account; quickly spot expired subscriptions or accounts in a grace period.
Under 'Platform' check system health in real time (BullMQ queues, Redis usage, API latency) to catch issues before they affect clients.

financials.title: How do I read the Platform Financials?
financials.description: Financials is the SaaS metrics panel exclusively for super admins: it shows MRR, ARR, churn, LTV, infrastructure costs, and per-tenant profitability. Use it to make decisions about pricing, plans, and operational cost optimization.
tips: The 'Overview' tab shows the current MRR and a 6-month projection — review it monthly to spot growth or decline trends.
In the 'Revenue' tab you'll see a breakdown by plan type (Starter, Pro, Enterprise, Custom); compare the number of trial vs. active tenants to measure conversion rate.
The 'Customers' tab includes a churn trend — if you see cancellation spikes in a given month, look into what happened around that date (price change, incident, etc.).
Under 'Costs' you can see infrastructure spending plus LLM cost per tenant; identify which tenants consume the most AI to adjust their plan limits.
Use the 'Refresh data' button (in the 'Settings' tab) to generate a manual monthly snapshot and keep the financial history up to date.

dashboard.title: What does the Dashboard show?
dashboard.description: The Dashboard is your business overview: new leads today, hot leads, messages processed by the AI, and how much it cost. Use it every morning to decide where to focus before diving into the rest of the platform.
tips: The 'Leads Today' counter shows new contacts for the day — if it looks low, check whether your WhatsApp or other channel is active under 'Channels'.
The 'AI Cost Today' figure updates in real time — if it exceeds your daily budget, switch the LLM model from the 'AI' section.
The 'Recent Activity' card color-codes events: green for conversations, orange for handoffs, indigo for orders — click a handoff row to jump straight to that chat in the Inbox.
The 'Model Usage' chart shows which LLM handled the most requests today and at what percentage — useful for checking whether your router is using the right tier.
If you see the yellow 'No channel connected' banner, click 'Connect channel' to go directly to the WhatsApp, Instagram, or Telegram setup page.

dripSequences.title: How do Drip Sequences work?
dripSequences.description: A drip sequence is a series of messages sent automatically to your leads over time, with configured delays between each one. Use it to nurture prospects who are not yet ready to buy, without having to write each message manually.
tips: Click '+ New Sequence' to create one; pick a trigger (e.g., 'Lead captured') and then add each step with its content and the wait time before the next message.
Enable or disable any sequence with the toggle switch without deleting it — handy if you want to pause it during holidays or special campaigns.
Check the 'Enrolled' counter on each card to see how many leads are in that flow right now; if the number grows very fast, make sure the stop conditions are properly configured.
Set stop conditions ('stop_if') so the sequence cancels automatically when a lead replies or changes stage — prevents messaging contacts who have already converted.
Use the 'AI generated' step type to let the agent compose the message based on the lead's context, instead of always sending the same fixed text.

automationTemplates.title: How do I install an automation template?
automationTemplates.description: Templates are ready-to-use automations grouped by category (nurturing, reminders, abandoned cart, welcome sequences, etc.) and industry (health, real estate, retail…). Use them to activate workflows in seconds without building from scratch.
tips: Use the search bar and the 'Category' and 'Industry' filters to narrow results; for example, filter by 'abandoned_cart' + 'retail' to recover lost sales.
Before installing, check the usage counter (trend icon) and the card description to understand exactly what the automation does.
Clicking 'Install' opens a modal showing the trigger, the number of actions, and configurable variables — adjust those variables to your business before confirming.
After installing, click 'View rules' in the success modal to go straight to the Automation page and activate or edit the newly created rule.
If you get no results, try clearing filters with 'Clear filters' — the full gallery includes universal templates that work for any industry.

crmAnalytics.title: How do I read the CRM Analytics?
crmAnalytics.description: CRM Analytics measures your business health: active opportunities, pipeline value, conversion rate, closing velocity, and agent performance. Use them to spot bottlenecks in your funnel and make data-driven decisions.
tips: In the 'Overview' tab, review the 5 top KPIs (total contacts, active opportunities, pipeline value, average score, and conversion rate) for a quick snapshot of your funnel.
In the 'Funnel' tab, use the horizontal bar chart by stage to see where leads accumulate most; a very crowded stage may indicate a follow-up bottleneck.
The 'Velocity' tab shows the average number of days a lead spends in each stage — if 'Qualified' has a high number, the team may need faster closing actions.
Check the Won/Lost analysis for your close rate and the most common loss reasons; those reasons tell you which objections to train your AI agent on.
In the 'Agents' tab, the leaderboard ranks your team by closed deals and total value — use it to recognize the top seller of the month or spot who needs support.

agentAnalytics.title: How do I evaluate your agents' performance?
agentAnalytics.description: This section shows performance metrics for each AI and human agent: conversations handled, first response time, resolution rate, and CSAT. Use it to identify who is performing best and where bottlenecks are forming.
tips: Change the date range with the selectors at the top to compare specific weeks or months.
In the 'Agents' tab, click a column header (e.g., 'Response Time') to sort and find the slowest agent.
The 'IA' badge (indigo) distinguishes automated agents from humans (green), so you compare like with like.
A CSAT in red (below 3.0) is a warning sign; review that agent's recent conversations to understand the cause.
Use the 'CSAT' tab to read customers' literal feedback and spot patterns that numbers alone don't reveal.

reportBuilder.title: How do I create and save custom reports?
reportBuilder.description: The Report Builder lets you combine up to 16 business metrics (conversations, AI cost, leads, appointments, CSAT, etc.) into a bar, line, area, or pie chart, for any date range you need. Use it to build the exact reports your team needs and save them for quick access.
tips: Click 'New report', pick metrics from the group you care about (e.g., 'AI' to see cost and resolution rate), then hit the eye icon to preview before saving.
Choose a chart type based on what you want to communicate: 'Bar' to compare periods, 'Line' to spot trends, 'Pie' to show proportions.
Click the star icon on any saved report to mark it as a favorite and find it quickly at the top of the list.
Use the 'Duplicate' button on an existing report to create a variant without deleting the original — handy for comparing different date ranges.
Adjust the date range inside the editor and press the eye icon to refresh the preview before saving your changes.

compliance.title: How do I manage privacy and legal compliance?
compliance.description: Compliance centralizes everything related to data protection: legal texts (policies, terms, consents), opt-out records, deletion requests, and a full audit log. Use it to comply with GDPR, LGPD, and local regulations without leaving anything to chance.
tips: In the 'Legal texts' tab, create a text of type 'Privacy policy' or 'Consent' and assign it to the right channels and agents using the selection chips — the agent will display it automatically.
Use the type filter (privacy, terms, AI disclosure, opt-in, etc.) to quickly find the text you want to edit or version; the version number increments automatically.
In the 'Opt-outs' tab, review pending items (red badge on the tab) and confirm or reject each one; confirming blocks the contact from future sends, rejecting marks it as a false positive.
When a customer requests data deletion, it appears in 'Deletion requests' with a pending status — click 'Process' to execute the deletion and leave a record in the system.
The 'Audit' tab logs every compliance action with its responsible user and timestamp; use it for any legal inquiry or internal review.

featureRequests.title: How do I suggest and vote on features?
featureRequests.description: The feature requests section is the direct channel between you and the Parallly product team: submit ideas, vote on others', and track each request's status from 'Open' to 'Shipped'. The more votes an idea gets, the higher it moves on the roadmap.
tips: Before submitting a new request, use the search bar to check if a similar idea already exists — the system automatically detects duplicates and shows you the match percentage.
Click the vote button (up arrow) on any card to add your vote; you can remove it later if you change your mind.
Filter by category (AI, Integrations, CRM, Analytics, etc.) or use the 'Top Voted' / 'Recent' sort selector to quickly find what you're looking for.
Switch to the 'Changelog' tab to see which requests from the board have already been shipped, grouped by the month they were released.
Open any request to read team comments or leave your own — replies marked as 'Team' come directly from the Parallly product team.

agentSimulation.title: How does agent simulation work?
agentSimulation.description: Simulation runs automated test conversations against your AI agent using synthetic scenarios or replays of real chats, and a judge evaluates each response across five dimensions. Use it before deploying major changes to catch regressions without affecting real customers.
tips: Choose 'Synthetic scenarios' to generate varied test cases automatically; choose 'Replay' to re-run real conversations that already happened on your channel.
Set 'Scenario count' between 1 and 100 depending on your time budget: 20 scenarios are enough for a quick check, 50 or more for thorough validation.
Select a 'Baseline' from the dropdown to compare the current result against a previous run; if the new score drops, you will see the 'Regression detected' alert with the affected scenarios listed.
Click any row in the scenarios table to open the side panel with the full transcript, sub-scores (Resolution, Tone, Accuracy, Empathy) and judge flags.
Check the 'History' section to track average score evolution over time and decide when the agent is ready for production.

attribution.title: How does revenue attribution work?
attribution.description: Attribution shows which Meta ads (Click-to-WhatsApp) and broadcast campaigns generated contacts, leads, and closed sales, measuring the real revenue each marketing action produced. Use it to decide where to invest your ad budget based on actual results, not just clicks.
tips: Switch the time range using the '30', '90', or '365' day buttons at the top to adjust the analysis period; for example, use 90 days to evaluate a quarterly campaign.
Review the top KPIs ('Ad clicks', 'Conversions', 'Attributed revenue', 'Leads generated') for a global summary before drilling into the per-ad breakdown.
In the 'By ad' table, compare the 'Conversion rate' column across ads: if an ad has many clicks but few closes, adjust its copy or targeting.
The 'Broadcast revenue' section shows how many sales each broadcast campaign generated; identify the highest-revenue campaign to replicate its message in the next one.
The visual funnel (Clicks → Contacts → Leads → Won) helps you spot the biggest drop-off; if the gap between 'Leads' and 'Won' is large, the problem may be in agent follow-up.

organizations.title: How do I manage companies and B2B opportunities?
organizations.description: Organizations is the CRM module for B2B sales: it groups your contacts under companies, records open opportunities per account, and projects weighted revenue based on funnel stage. Use it when you sell to businesses (not just individuals) and need to see the total value of each account in one place.
tips: Click '+ New organization' to create a company; fill in at least the name and industry so filters and reports work correctly.
Use the search box in the 'Organizations' section to find a company by name; for example, type 'Acme' and all matching accounts will appear.
Review the top KPIs ('Weighted pipeline', 'Committed', 'Best case', 'Average velocity') for a quarterly revenue projection without manually checking each opportunity.
The 'By stage' section shows the total value bar and probability-weighted value for each stage; if 'Proposal sent' holds a lot of value without progressing, that is a signal to follow up.
When a card appears in the 'Stale deals alerts' section it has had no activity for over 14 days; prioritize those opportunities in your calendar to avoid losing them.

coupons.title: How do I create and manage discount coupons?
coupons.description: Coupons are discount codes you can create and distribute to customers or partners to reduce the price of Parallly plans; they support three types: percentage off, fixed amount, and free months. This section is exclusive to super admins and lets you control expiry, usage limits, and which plans each coupon applies to.
tips: Click 'Create coupon' and enter an uppercase code without spaces (for example, 'LAUNCH50') to make it easy to share and remember.

Choose the coupon type based on your strategy: 'Percentage off' for relative discounts (for example, 20% off), 'Fixed amount' to subtract an exact amount (for example, $10), or 'Free months' to gift full subscription periods.
Use the 'Max redemptions' field to cap availability; for example, set 50 if it is a launch promotion that should not exceed that number of uses.
Set an 'Expiry date' for time-limited campaign coupons; the code will stop working automatically on the chosen date without requiring manual deactivation.

When a coupon should no longer accept new uses, click the 'Deactivate' icon (red button in the row) to mark it as inactive without deleting it; this preserves the redemption history in the 'Uses' column.

identity.title: How does contact identity merging work?
identity.description: Identity automatically detects when the same customer contacted you from different channels (for example, WhatsApp and Instagram) and suggests merging those profiles into one, preventing duplicates in your CRM. You can also merge two contacts manually if the system did not detect them automatically.
tips: In the 'Suggestions' tab, review pending cards and check the match reason (for example, 'Phone match' or 'Email match') and confidence percentage before approving.
Click 'Approve' if the two profiles are the same person; the system will unify their conversation history and contact data into a single record.
Click 'Reject' if the contacts are different people even though they share a phone or email; this prevents the system from suggesting them together again.

If the system did not detect the duplicate automatically, use the 'Manual merge' tab: search for the first contact in the list, select it as 'A', then search for the second and select it as 'B', and confirm the merge.
The 'Pending', 'Approved', and 'Rejected' counters at the top show the overall status of your suggestions; if 'Pending' keeps growing, consider scheduling weekly time to review them.

inventory.title: How do I manage inventory?
inventory.description: Inventory is your product catalog with real-time stock control: see how many units you have, their total value, and which items need restocking. Use it to avoid selling out-of-stock items and to log every stock movement.
tips: Check the 'Low stock' and 'Out of stock' KPI cards at the top; if either shows a number in orange or red, click 'Adjust stock' on that product before the AI agent offers it to customers.
Filter by category using the color-coded buttons to view only one product line at a time; for example, select 'Electronics' to compare prices and stock without scrolling through everything.
Search by product name or SKU in the search field; if you manage 200 SKUs and need to update 'CAM-001', just type it instead of browsing the full list.
When logging a stock adjustment, choose the right type: 'In' (+) for supplier deliveries, 'Out' (−) for off-system sales, and 'Adjustment' to correct the total after a physical count.
Add the cost when creating a product so the panel can automatically calculate the estimated profit margin shown below the 'Inventory value' KPI.

managed.title: How does the managed service work?
managed.description: The 'Managed' section is a super-admin-only panel for tracking the resolution guarantee you offer your clients: you set a target percentage of AI-resolved conversations and the system shows whether each account is meeting it. Use it to spot accounts that are at risk or have already breached their service agreement.
tips: To enroll an account, select the tenant in the 'Add account' selector, enter the target percentage (e.g. 80%) in the 'Target %' field, and click 'Enable'; the system will then start comparing real results against that goal.

Watch the 'Status' column: 'Met' (green) means the verified rate exceeds the target, 'At risk' (amber) means it is close to the limit, and 'Breached' (red) means the gap is already over the threshold.

The 'Verified rate' column shows the percentage of conversations where the AI resolved the issue and that resolution was confirmed; it is stricter than the overall rate, so use it as the real service benchmark.
Adjust the target directly in the table by editing the numeric field in that row; the change saves automatically when you click away, no button needed.
If an account no longer needs managed service, click 'Disable' at the end of its row; the account disappears from tracking but historical data is preserved.

orders.title: How do I manage orders?
orders.description: Orders are purchase transactions created by your customers or manually by your team: you can see the full history, the total amount receivable, and each transaction's status (pending, confirmed, paid, or cancelled). Use it to track cash flow and ensure no sale goes unprocessed.
tips: Filter orders by status using the buttons in the top bar; for example, click 'Pending' to see only orders awaiting payment and prioritize collections for the day.
Change an order's status directly from the selector in the 'Quick action' column; when you confirm a bank transfer, switch it from 'Pending' to 'Paid' without opening any detail view.
Generate and open any order's invoice with the 'View receipt' button; it opens in a new tab as printable HTML ready to share with the customer.
Search for an order by customer name or order ID in the search field; if a customer messages on WhatsApp asking about their order, find it in seconds.
When creating an order manually, select available-stock products from the 'Add products' dropdown and adjust quantities; the total is calculated in real time before you confirm.

procedures.title: How do I create and use procedures (SOPs)?
procedures.description: Procedures are step-by-step conversation flows that the AI agent runs automatically when it detects certain trigger keywords: you define what message to send, what question to ask, what tool to call, what condition to evaluate, or when to hand off to a human agent. Use them to standardize complex responses without the agent improvising.
tips: Use the 'Write SOP' button to describe the procedure in plain language (as if explaining to a new employee) and let the AI compile it into structured steps automatically; for example, write 'First ask for the name, then check availability, if in stock confirm the order'.

In the editor, add an 'Ask' step whenever you need to capture a data point from the customer, like their email or appointment number; the 'Field' input defines the variable name where the answer is stored.

Use 'Condition' steps to branch the flow based on the customer's response; for example, if the 'budget' field is greater than 500,000, continue to the closing step, otherwise show budget-friendly options.
Define 'Trigger keywords' separated by commas so the procedure activates when the customer mentions those phrases; for example: 'quote, price, how much' triggers the pricing flow.

Toggle the procedure status with the 'Activate' or 'Deactivate' button as needed; a procedure in 'Draft' status does not run even if the customer types the trigger keywords, so use it to test before publishing.

verticalAnalytics.title: How do I analyze performance by industry?
verticalAnalytics.description: Vertical analytics is a super-admin-only panel showing how all platform tenants are distributed by industry (health, restaurants, tourism, real estate, etc.) and their activation and payment status. Use it to identify which verticals have the most traction and which accounts still have incomplete setups.
tips: In the 'Overview' tab, click any industry bar to jump directly to that vertical's detail in the 'Drilldown' tab; for example, click 'Tourism' to see all tenants in that sector with their individual metrics.

Review the 'Activation gaps' table in the 'Overview' tab: it shows registered tenants that have no connected channel or configured agent; click the tenant name to go to their profile and help them complete setup.
In the 'Drilldown' tab, select an industry from the buttons at the top to see that sector's tenant ranking ordered by activation level and recent activity.
Use the 'Refresh' button (top right) to force a real-time data reload if you just created or activated tenants and the KPIs do not yet reflect those changes.

In the 'Drilldown' tenant ranking table, the 'Activated' column with a green dot means that tenant already sent their first message; empty circles indicate no real conversations yet, and those tenants may need onboarding support.

audit.title: What is the audit log for?
audit.description: The audit log records every important action on the platform, such as channel connections, suspensions, and billing events. Use it to trace who did what and when, without needing to dig into server logs.
tips: Filter by 'Tenant' by typing the UUID or name to see only that tenant's actions, e.g. type 'acme' in the tenant search field.
Use the 'Action' filter with keywords like 'disconnect' or 'reactivate' to quickly find critical events.
Set a start date with 'Since' to narrow the search to recent incidents, e.g. the day of an outage.
Click any row in the table to expand it and view the full JSON with event details.
Use the 'Previous' / 'Next' buttons at the bottom to browse pages; each page shows 100 records.

catalog.title: What can I manage from the Catalog?
catalog.description: The Catalog is the central hub where you organize your business offer: courses, marketing campaigns, and promotions. From here you can access each section with a single click to manage your complete portfolio.
tips: Click the 'Courses' card to manage your educational offer: create, edit and activate courses with price and modality.
Use the 'Campaigns' card to create marketing campaigns linked to your courses and WhatsApp or Email channels.
The 'Offers' card takes you to active promotions the AI agent can mention during conversations.
Navigate between sections using the cards — each one shows a short description to guide you.
Return to this page anytime from the 'Catalog' item in the sidebar for an overall view.

campaigns.title: How do catalog campaigns work?
campaigns.description: Campaigns are the mechanism for capturing leads and guiding them toward a course or offer through channels like WhatsApp or Email. Each campaign defines the channel, message template, and lead entry source.
tips: Click 'New Campaign' to create one; assign a clear name like 'June 2026 Admissions' for easy identification.
Select 'Main Course' in the modal to link the campaign to a catalog course — only already-registered courses appear.
Choose the 'Entry Source' based on how leads will arrive: 'Landing Page', 'CSV Import', 'Meta Lead Ads', etc.
If using WhatsApp, fill in the 'WhatsApp Template' field with the exact name of the Meta-approved template.
Enable 'email fallback' if you want the platform to try email contact when the WhatsApp message fails.

catalogCourses.title: How do I manage courses in the catalog?
catalogCourses.description: The course catalog is where you register your full educational offer with price, modality and duration so the AI agent can present it to prospects. From here you create, edit and control the availability of each course.
tips: Click 'New Course' to add a course; fill in at least the name and price so the agent has useful information.
Use the 'Slug (URL)' field with a short identifier like 'marketing-diploma' — it is auto-generated if left empty.
Set the 'Modality': 'In-person', 'Virtual' or 'Hybrid'; the AI agent will use this data when answering prospect questions.
Add the brochure URL in 'Brochure URL' so the agent can share the document when a lead requests it.
Check the 'Active' counter in the top stats to see how many courses are currently available to the agent.

offers.title: How do catalog offers work?
offers.description: Offers are promotions (discounts, promos or bundles) that your AI agent can communicate to customers. Set validity dates and conditions so they only activate at the right time.
tips: Click 'New offer' to create a promotion; choose between 'Discount', 'Promo' or 'Bundle' depending on your sales strategy.
Fill in 'Valid from' and 'Valid to' so the offer is automatically marked as active (green badge) only during the configured period.
In the 'Conditions' field enter a valid JSON with the offer parameters, for example: {"discount_pct": 20, "code": "SUMMER20"}.
Uncheck 'Active' to keep an offer as a draft without the agent using it yet.
Edit any existing offer with the pencil icon; changes are immediately reflected in agent responses.

complianceAdmin.title: What can I manage from Compliance Admin?
complianceAdmin.description: This panel centralizes compliance requests (GDPR/LGPD) across all platform tenants. As a super admin you can monitor pending deletions, recent opt-outs and export data for any contact.
tips: Check the 'Deletions' tab regularly: if the red counter exceeds 0, there are pending deletion requests you must process to meet Article 17 GDPR deadlines.
In the 'Opt-outs' tab click on a tenant name to navigate directly to its tenant profile and take action.
To export contact data (Article 15), go to the 'Export' tab, enter the tenant UUID and contact UUID, and download the resulting JSON.
Use the 'Refresh' button in the top-right corner to update request status without reloading the page.
Status badges in 'Opt-outs' change color by result: green = confirmed, red = rejected, yellow = pending.

segments.title: What are contact segments for?
segments.description: Segments are groups of contacts automatically formed by rules you define (stage, score, channel, etc.). Use them to send targeted campaigns or analyze specific groups of leads.
tips: Create a segment with 'New segment' and combine multiple filters; for example, 'stage = qualified' + 'score >= 70' to identify leads ready to close.
Before saving, click the eye icon 'Preview' to see how many contacts match the current filters and adjust criteria if the number is too high or too low.
Click any segment in the list to see the contact table with name, phone, email, stage and score.
Use the 'in' operator to filter by multiple values at once; for example, in the 'stage' field enter 'prospect,qualified' separated by commas.
The contact counter on each segment card updates every time you load the page, so you always see the real current total.

conversations.title: How do I explore all conversations?
conversations.description: This view shows all active, waiting, resolved and handoff conversations for your tenant in a single table. Use it to get a global picture of service status and spot conversations that need immediate attention.
tips: Filter by status using the 'All / Active / Waiting / Resolved' selector to focus on the most urgent conversations; 'Waiting' status usually means the customer is waiting for a reply.
Use the search bar to find a conversation by contact name, phone number or a fragment of the last message.
Toggle the sort order with the 'Recent / Most messages' button to prioritize highly active conversations and spot engaged leads.
Check the 'Sentiment' column (emoji) to quickly identify contacts with negative sentiment and prioritize their care.
The 'Most used tags' section at the bottom shows which tags appear most often; use them to detect recurring topics across conversations.

funnel.title: How does the conversion funnel work?
funnel.description: The funnel shows how many tenants advance from signup to payment, stage by stage. Use it to identify where the most volume is lost and prioritize activation actions.
tips: Use the '7d', '30d', and '90d' buttons to compare periods: if the 7d funnel shows worse conversion than the 30d one, there may be a recent onboarding issue.
The 'Conversion' column in the 'By source' table tells you which acquisition channel brings tenants who actually pay. Focus your marketing efforts there.
The 'Time to first message' (TTFM) metric measures how quickly a tenant activates their agent. A value over 48h suggests the onboarding flow is too complex.
If the 'Onboarding completed' bar drops more than 30% compared to 'Signups', review the setup wizard — a blocking step may be stopping users.
Click 'Refresh' after a product change to see the impact in real time without waiting for the automatic cycle.

health.title: What does this health panel show?
health.description: The panel displays the real-time status of core services (API, Redis, Postgres) and the job volume in each BullMQ queue. Use it to detect degradations before they impact tenants.
tips: The status banner (green/yellow/red) summarizes the overall diagnosis: yellow means there are failed jobs in some queue even if services are active. Check rows with red numbers.
Click any number in the 'Failed' column to open the inspector and see the exact error reason for each job. From there, use 'Retry' to requeue it.
If the 'Delayed' column shows high values (>100) in a queue, there may be a bottleneck in the processor. Review the corresponding worker logs.
Use 'Clean all' in the inspector (filtering by 'older than 24h') to purge accumulated failed jobs without deleting recent ones that could still be retried.
The page auto-refreshes every 15 seconds; no need to reload manually unless you want immediate data after an action.

faqs.title: How to manage frequently asked questions?
faqs.description: FAQs are predefined answers that the AI agent can use directly when a customer asks a common question. Keeping them up to date reduces model hallucinations and improves accuracy.
tips: Click 'New FAQ' to create an entry. Fill in at least 'Question' and 'Answer'; the 'Category' and 'Tags' fields are optional but help organize content as volume grows.
Use the 'Category' field with consistent names (e.g., 'Pricing', 'Shipping') so FAQs appear grouped in the list, making them easier to find when editing.
The 'Tags' field accepts comma-separated values (e.g., 'return, refund, warranty'). The RAG search engine uses them to retrieve the correct FAQ for variations of the same question.
Uncheck the 'Published' toggle if you are drafting or reviewing an answer: the FAQ won't be considered by the agent until you publish it again.
The 'views' counter on each card tells you which questions the agent receives most. Prioritize keeping high-traffic FAQs up to date.

landings.title: What are landing pages for?
landings.description: Landing pages are public lead capture pages linked to courses and campaigns. Each page has its own URL with a slug and can be published or kept as a draft.
tips: Use the search bar at the top to filter pages by title or slug. If you have many, type the first letters of the name to quickly find the one you want to edit.

When creating a new page with 'New Landing', the slug (public URL) is generated automatically if you leave it empty. To customize the URL, type it in the 'Slug' field using only letters, numbers, and hyphens.
Link the page to a 'Course' or 'Campaign' during creation so captured leads are automatically associated with the correct funnel.
The status indicator on each card can be 'draft' (yellow dot) or 'published' (green dot). Only published pages are accessible from the public URL.
Click 'View Landing' on the card to open the public page in a new tab and verify how visitors see it before sharing the link.

llmStats.title: What are AI Stats?
llmStats.description: This screen shows the cost and volume of all AI model calls (LLM, media, and embeddings) grouped by month, category, provider, and tenant. It helps you spot which tenant or provider drives the most spend so you can optimize costs.
tips: Switch the range with the '1M / 3M / 6M / 12M' buttons to see short- or long-term trends: use '1M' for immediate diagnosis and '12M' for annual planning.
In the 'By provider' section, compare 'Tokens' and 'Cost' columns between openai and anthropic to pick the most efficient provider for each task type.
The 'Top tenants' table shows who spends the most: click a tenant name to go to their detail and verify whether their plan covers actual consumption.
If the 'LLM' (indigo) bar dominates the monthly chart, check whether the LLM tier assigned to that tenant's plan matches their usage level (Starter should not use tier_3).
Hit 'Refresh' after changing the date range to force an immediate reload without waiting for the next automatic cycle.

plans.title: How to manage subscription plans?
plans.description: This screen shows the comparison table for all plans (Starter, Pro, Enterprise, Custom) with their limits, features, and prices. You can edit any parameter here and the change automatically propagates to active tenants on that plan.
tips: Click the pencil icon on a plan's column header to enter edit mode; fields become editable without reloading the page.
After editing, click the save icon in the plan header: the system invalidates the cache for all tenants on that plan and shows how many were updated.
To change enabled channels (whatsapp, instagram, messenger, telegram, sms), toggle the colored chips in the 'Channels' row while in edit mode.
Use the 'Invalidate cache' section at the bottom of the page to force a specific plan's update without changing its values — useful after infrastructure changes.
Check the 'Tenants' count in each plan header before reducing limits: if there are active tenants, notify them before saving to avoid service disruptions.

usage.title: What is the Platform Usage panel for?
usage.description: This screen shows the actual consumption of automations and outbound messages for each active tenant against their plan limits. It helps you identify who is approaching their quota so you can upgrade their plan or reach out proactively.
tips: Click the 'Automations' or 'Outbound' column headers to sort the table by usage percentage descending and immediately see the tenants closest to their limit.
A red bar means the tenant has already exceeded their quota (100%); an amber bar signals usage between 80% and 99%: act before their messages get blocked.
Use the search field to filter by tenant name or plan (e.g. type 'pro' to see only Pro tenants and compare their consumption against each other).
The 'Over quota' tile at the top shows how many tenants are at 100%: if it's greater than zero, prioritize contacting them to prevent churn.
Click a tenant name in the table to go to their detail at '/admin/tenants' and from there change their plan or review their billing history.

ops.title: What is the Operations Center?
ops.description: It's the central NOC panel that summarizes the whole platform's health in one view: active incidents, service and queue status, storage usage, and quick links to each detailed panel. It's the starting point to detect and act on any problem.
tips: The top banner summarizes overall status: green (operational), amber (needs attention) or red (critical). Red means a critical incident or a service down.
The incident tiles are clickable — they take you to /admin/incidents to acknowledge or resolve.
'System vitals' shows API/PostgreSQL/Redis and the BullMQ queues; a red dot or failed jobs signal a problem.
The storage section shows disk % and the fill projection; act before it reaches 90%.
This view auto-refreshes every 30s; use the quick links to drill into any area.

incidents.title: What is the Incidents panel?
incidents.description: It's the ops center's alert inbox. Every detected problem (disk, RAM, Redis, queues, AI providers, disk projection, per-tenant quota, payments, tokens...) is recorded here persistently, with how many times it recurred and since when. Previously they only arrived by email and were lost on restart.
tips: Start with 'Active critical' — those need immediate action. The red number at the top tells you how many there are.
Use 'Acknowledge' to mark that you're aware of an incident (it stays active but stops being noise); use 'Resolve' once the problem is fixed.
Many incidents resolve themselves: when the condition returns to normal (e.g. disk drops below 80%) the system marks them resolved automatically.
The ×N counter shows how many times the same alert recurred without resolving: a high number signals a persistent problem.
The 'Resolved' filter is your history: use it to see what happened in the last 24h and spot recurring patterns.

storage.title: What is the Storage panel for?
storage.description: This screen shows how much storage each tenant consumes: their database size (conversations, messages, embeddings) and media files on disk, plus the server's total disk usage. It helps you spot who is growing too fast and act before the disk fills up.
tips: The 'Server disk usage' bar turns amber at 80% and red at 90%: if it gets there, free space or expand the disk before writes get blocked.
Sort the table by 'Total' to instantly see which tenants consume the most storage; sort by 'Media quota' to see who is close to their plan limit.
The 'Near quota' tile counts tenants at 80%+ of their media quota: reach out to upgrade their plan before they can no longer upload files.
Use 'Analyze' in Clean orphaned files to see how much reclaimable space exists without deleting anything; the delete button only appears afterward.
Click a tenant's name to open its detail and adjust its quota (mediaStorageMb) or change its plan.

webhooks.title: What is the Webhook monitor?
webhooks.description: This screen is a real-time monitoring console (updates every 5 seconds) showing the last 200 webhook events received from all channels. It is used to debug integrations and detect errors without needing server access.
tips: Use the channel filters (whatsapp, instagram, messenger, telegram, sms) and status filters (parsed, ignored, error, rejected) to isolate exactly the events you need: e.g. select 'whatsapp' + 'error' to see only WhatsApp failures.
Click 'Pause' to stop automatic updates and read events calmly; when done, click 'Resume' to return to live mode.
The summary tiles (Parsed / Ignored / Rejected / Error) show counts from the current batch: if 'Error' is greater than zero, review the red events in the list to find the exact error message.
Each row shows a relative time (e.g. '12s', '3m') in the right column: very recent events with 'error' status are the highest priority to investigate.
The system stores only summaries (no PII or full payloads): if you need the full payload, use the API container logs with the accountId shown in the row.

settingsAiConfig.title: How to configure global AI model behavior?
settingsAiConfig.description: This section controls the parameters the AI router uses when it cannot automatically decide which model to apply. Adjusting these values impacts the cost, speed, and creativity of all your agents' responses.
tips: Choose the 'Default model' based on your priority: 'gpt-4o-mini' is cheaper and faster; 'gpt-4o' or 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514' handle complex conversations better.
Set 'Temperature' between 0.3 and 0.5 for precise sales responses. Raise it to 0.7 if you want the agent to sound more natural and varied.
Set 'Max Tokens' to 400-600 for concise WhatsApp replies. Raise it to 1200+ only if your agents handle long content like quotes or detailed FAQs.
After changing any value, press 'Save' — the button turns green with a checkmark when changes are applied successfully.

settingsAiProviders.title: How to connect AI provider API keys?
settingsAiProviders.description: Here you configure the secret keys for each model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, xAI, DeepSeek) that the platform uses to generate responses. Without at least one valid key, your agents cannot work.
tips: Paste the key into the corresponding provider field — for example, an OpenAI key starts with 'sk-'. The eye icon lets you verify you copied it completely before saving.
When a key is saved, a green 'Configured' badge appears on the provider card. If it doesn't appear, the key hasn't been registered yet.
You can load keys from multiple providers simultaneously — the AI router will select the most suitable one based on plan and task. Having at least OpenAI + one additional is recommended.
After pasting all keys, press the 'Save' button in the top right corner. Keys are stored encrypted — they are never shown in full text after saving.

settingsAlerts.title: How to configure alerts and automated reports?
settingsAlerts.description: This section lets you create rules that send automatic emails when a metric exceeds a threshold (e.g., active conversations > 50) and schedule periodic reports with a summary of your account activity.
tips: Click '+ New alert', assign a descriptive name like 'Queue saturated', choose the metric 'queue_depth', operator '>' and threshold '20' — so you know when too many conversations are waiting.
In 'Notification emails', separate multiple recipients with commas: e.g., 'manager@company.com, support@company.com'. The field accepts up to 5 addresses.
Set 'Cooldown' to at least 60 minutes to avoid alert spam if the metric fluctuates. For critical alerts like LLM costs, use 30 minutes.
In the 'Scheduled reports' section, enable the 'Active' toggle, select frequency 'Weekly' or 'Monthly', enter recipients and save — you'll receive an automatic summary without doing anything else.

settingsApiKeys.title: How to create and manage public API keys?
settingsApiKeys.description: API Keys allow you to connect external systems (CRM, ERP, custom integrations) to Parallly without exposing your user credentials. Each key has specific permissions (scopes) that limit what operations it can perform.
tips: Click 'Create key', type a name like 'CRM-Salesforce', select only the scopes you need (e.g., 'Read contacts' + 'Write messages') and save — you'll see the full key only once, copy it immediately.
Use 'Rotate' to replace a compromised key without removing its permissions — the system generates a new one and the old key stops working instantly.
When a key is no longer needed, use 'Revoke' (red button) to permanently delete it. Confirm in the modal — this action cannot be undone.
In each request header, use the exact format: 'Authorization: Bearer pk_live_YOUR_KEY' against the base endpoint 'https://api.parallly-chat.cloud/api/v1'.

settingsAppearance.title: How to change the dashboard visual theme?
settingsAppearance.description: Here you can adjust the visual appearance of the interface by choosing between light, dark, or automatic mode based on the operating system. The change applies immediately across the entire platform without needing to reload.
tips: Click the 'Dark' card to enable dark mode — ideal if you work long hours in front of a screen or in low-light environments. The blue checkmark indicates the active theme.
Choose 'System' so the dashboard automatically follows your device's light/dark mode — useful if you use the platform on both computer and phone.
Use the 'Component preview' section to see how buttons, cards, and badges look with your chosen theme before confirming your preference.
The 'Graphite' and 'Midnight' themes appear locked with the 'Coming soon' badge — they will be available in future versions. For now, the three active themes cover all use cases.

settingsBilling.title: How do I manage my subscription and payments?
settingsBilling.description: Here you control your current plan, monthly AI message usage, and payment history. You can change plans, update your card, or redeem a coupon from this page.
tips: If your usage bar exceeds 80%, click 'Upgrade now' to move to a higher plan before your messages run out.
To update your credit card, use the 'Change card' button in your active plan section.
If you have a promo code, enter it in the 'Redeem coupon' field (e.g. LAUNCH50) and press 'Redeem'.
Download individual invoices from the 'Payment history' table by clicking 'Download'.

settingsBusinessHours.title: How do I configure the bot's business hours?
settingsBusinessHours.description: Define which days and times your AI agent responds to messages. Outside those hours, a custom message is automatically sent to your customers.
tips: Enable the '24/7' toggle if you want the bot to respond at any time without schedule restrictions.
Select the correct timezone (e.g. 'America/Bogota') so hours are applied accurately to your country.
Enable or disable individual days using each row's toggle; adjust open and close times with the time fields.
Write an out-of-hours message in the bottom field (e.g. 'Hi! We respond Monday to Friday from 8am to 6pm.') and save changes.

settingsBusinessInfo.title: Why is it important to complete my company information?
settingsBusinessInfo.description: Your company information is used by the AI agent to answer questions about your business. A complete profile improves the accuracy and credibility of responses.
tips: The 'Company name' field is required; use the name your customers recognize (e.g. 'Smile Dental Clinic').
Upload your logo by clicking the dotted area or switch to 'URL' mode to paste an external link like 'https://cdn.example.com/logo.png'.
Fill in the 'Phone' and 'Email' fields so the bot can share them when a customer asks.
Add your social networks in the 'Social media' section (e.g. Instagram, Facebook) so the agent can mention them in responses.

settingsChangePassword.title: How do I change my password safely?
settingsChangePassword.description: From here you can update your account password. If you signed in with Google, you can also set an additional password to log in with email and password.
tips: Enter your current password in the first field; if you don't remember it, sign out and use the 'Forgot your password?' option.
Your new password must meet all requirements shown in the checklist (uppercase, number, special character, minimum 8 characters).
Use the eye icon to the right of each field to show or hide what you type and avoid typing errors.
If your account is Google-only, you can set an additional password without needing to enter a current password.

settingsChannels.title: How do I configure my messaging channel credentials?
settingsChannels.description: Here you enter the API keys and tokens to connect WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, and Telegram. These credentials allow the bot to send and receive messages on each channel.
tips: Select the tab for the channel you want to configure (e.g. 'WhatsApp') and fill in the 'Phone Number ID' and 'Access Token' from Meta Business.
Password-type fields (marked with a lock icon) are hidden by default; use the eye icon to reveal them and verify you pasted the correct value.
For Telegram, get the 'Bot Token' from @BotFather on Telegram and paste it in the corresponding field (e.g. '1234567890:AAHfiqk...').
The 'Webhook URL' for each channel is pre-filled; copy and paste it into the Meta or Telegram developer settings so messages arrive correctly.

settingsCompany.title: How do I set up my company information?
settingsCompany.description: Here you define your business general data: name, industry, size, website, and support contact. This information is used in email templates and in your AI agents' identity.
tips: Fill in the 'Industry' field so the system tailors suggestions to your business type (e.g. choose 'Health' for clinics).
The 'Support email' appears in automatic emails sent to your customers; use a real mailbox your team monitors.
To add or change your company logo, click the 'Media bank' link at the bottom of the form.
After editing any field, press 'Save changes' — the button turns green with a checkmark when the operation succeeds.

settingsCustomAttributes.title: What are custom attributes for?
settingsCustomAttributes.description: Custom attributes are extra fields you define to enrich information for your contacts, leads, companies, or conversations. They let you store business-specific data that doesn't exist by default.
tips: Use the 'Contact', 'Lead', 'Company', and 'Conversation' tabs to view and create attributes per entity; each tab shows only that type's fields.
When creating an attribute, the 'Key' is auto-generated from the 'Label' (e.g. 'Birth date' → 'birth_date'); you can edit it manually if you need a different name.
Choose the 'List' type if you want a closed-options field; type options separated by commas (e.g. 'Premium, Standard, Basic').
Enable 'Required field' only for truly mandatory data; required fields block saving when left empty.

settingsEmailTemplates.title: How do I create and use email templates?
settingsEmailTemplates.description: Email templates are reusable messages with dynamic variables that the system sends automatically (appointment confirmations, reminders, welcomes, etc.). You can create them from scratch or start from a preset.
tips: Click 'Create from template' to choose from 6 pre-designed models (Appointment Confirmation, Reminder, Booking, Check-in, Welcome, Team Notification) and start with the HTML already built.
Insert variables like '{{customer_name}}' or '{{appointment_date}}' by clicking the 'Available variables' chips; they insert at your cursor position.
Use the 'Preview' panel to see the email rendered with sample data before saving; switch to the 'HTML' tab to review the code.
Once the template is saved, use the 'Send test' button to receive the real email in your inbox and validate the design.

settingsIntegrations.title: How do I connect external integrations?
settingsIntegrations.description: Integrations let you connect Parallly with external tools like CRMs, vertical platforms, and MCP servers. Each integration automatically syncs data between systems.
tips: Go to the 'CRM' section to connect HubSpot, Pipedrive, or Kommo via OAuth; the process takes less than a minute.
Use the 'Test' button on an active integration to verify the connection still works before launching a campaign.
If an integration shows an error status, click 'Disconnect' and reconnect to renew the access token.
Vertical integrations (Toast, Mindbody, Cliniko) are available in the 'Vertical' subsection for specific industries.

settingsIntegrationsCrm.title: How do I sync my external CRM with Parallly?
settingsIntegrationsCrm.description: Here you connect Parallly with your external CRM (HubSpot, Pipedrive, or Kommo) to keep contacts and conversations synchronized between both systems in real time.
tips: Click 'Connect' on the card of the provider you use; the CRM OAuth flow opens and in less than a minute the integration is active.
Once connected, use the 'Test' button to validate the API responds correctly — if an error appears, disconnect and re-authorize.
Use 'Import' to bring your existing CRM contacts into Parallly; the system shows a preview with counts of new, matched, and invalid records before you confirm.
If the 'Last sync' column is empty or very old, disconnect and reconnect to force a fresh synchronization.

settingsIntegrationsMcp.title: What are MCP servers?
settingsIntegrationsMcp.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets you connect the AI agent to external tools via compatible servers. Use it so your agent can query APIs, databases, or your own services in real time during a conversation.
tips: Copy your MCP endpoint URL (the 'Your MCP endpoint' block) and paste it into the external client you want to connect — include the authorization header to secure it.
To add an external server, fill in the 'Name', 'URL', and 'Auth header' fields and click 'Add server'. You will see the green indicator when it is active.
Use the 'Test' button on each server to verify the connection before enabling it in production — it shows the number of available tools if everything is correct.
You can pause a server with the power icon without deleting it; the indicator turns gray and the agent temporarily stops using it.

settingsIntegrationsReviews.title: How does review management work?
settingsIntegrationsReviews.description: This section connects your Google Business Profile account to view and reply to reviews directly from the dashboard. The AI can suggest personalized responses and publish them to Google automatically if you enable the option.
tips: Click 'Connect Google Business' to start the OAuth flow; you need administrator access to the Google My Business account.
Enable 'Auto-reply' (the checkbox next to 'Sync') so the AI responds to new reviews without manual intervention — ideal for high volumes.
On each unanswered review, use 'AI Suggestion' to generate a draft based on the customer's comment; you can edit it before publishing with 'Post reply'.
Use 'Sync' to pull the latest reviews from Google at any time; the 'Unreplied' and 'Negative' counters help you prioritize.

settingsIntegrationsSlack.title: What is the Slack integration for?
settingsIntegrationsSlack.description: Connect Parallly to a Slack channel to receive automatic notifications when key events occur in the system. This way your team is instantly informed without having to check the dashboard manually.
tips: Create an Incoming Webhook in your Slack workspace (Slack App Directory → 'Incoming WebHooks') and paste the URL starting with 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/...' into the 'Webhook URL' field.
Check 'Handoff to agent' to receive a Slack alert every time the bot transfers a conversation to a human agent — useful for fast response.
Enable 'New appointment' so the team sees each booking confirmed by the AI agent in Slack without opening the Appointments module.
Use 'Send test message' after saving to verify the webhook works correctly before enabling it in production.

settingsIntegrationsVertical.title: What are vertical integrations?
settingsIntegrationsVertical.description: Connect Parallly with industry-specific software (Toast for restaurants, Mindbody for gyms/wellness, Cliniko for clinics) so the agent can check availability, book appointments, and sync data in real time.
tips: To connect Toast, enter the 'Hostname', 'Client ID', 'Client Secret', and 'Restaurant GUID' from your Toast developer account (available at developer.toasttab.com).
For Cliniko, the 'Base URL (shard)' field depends on your region: Australia uses 'https://api.au1.cliniko.com/v1' and other regions have their own subdomain.
Once connected, use 'Test' to verify that the credentials work — you will see a success message if the API responds correctly.
Use 'Sync' after connecting to import available services, schedules, or practitioners; the count of synced records appears as confirmation.

settingsIntegrationsWebChat.title: How to install the chat widget on your website?
settingsIntegrationsWebChat.description: The chat widget embeds the AI agent on any website with a JavaScript snippet. You can customize colors, position, welcome message, and pre-chat form, then copy the code to paste into your HTML.
tips: Click 'Create widget' to generate a new widget; then use the gear icon to configure the name, color (color picker), position ('Bottom right' / 'Bottom left'), and welcome message.
Enable the 'Pre-chat form' with the toggle in the edit section to ask visitors for their name, email, or other data before starting the conversation.
Copy the code snippet with the '</>' icon and paste it before the closing '</body>' tag on your site — the widget will appear automatically for all visitors.
Use the 'Triggers' button to define automatic appearance rules (for example, show the chat after 30 seconds or on specific pages) without any extra code.

settingsIntegrationsWebChatTriggers.title: How do widget triggers work?
settingsIntegrationsWebChatTriggers.description: Triggers are automatic rules that open or show the chat widget when a visitor meets certain conditions. Use them to start conversations at the right moment and boost engagement.
tips: Combine conditions: use 'Time on page' (e.g. 30 seconds) with 'Page URL' (e.g. '/pricing') to fire the widget only when someone has spent time on your pricing page.
Use 'Exit intent' to show a retention message (e.g. 'Leaving? We have a special offer') right before the visitor closes the tab.
Set 'Frequency' to 60 minutes or more to avoid showing the same message repeatedly to a visitor browsing multiple pages.
Assign lower priority numbers to your most important triggers; the system runs the highest-priority one first.

settingsIntegrationsWebhooks.title: What are outbound webhooks for?
settingsIntegrationsWebhooks.description: Webhooks send event data from your account (new leads, appointments, handoffs) to an external URL in real time. Use them to connect Parallly with your CRM, ERP, or other tools without polling.
tips: When creating an endpoint, select only the events you need (e.g. 'lead.created' and 'appointment.booked') to avoid unnecessary traffic to your server.
Use the 'Send test' button (airplane icon) to verify your server receives and processes the payload correctly before activating the webhook in production.
Verify each call's authenticity using the HMAC-SHA256 signature in the 'X-Webhook-Signature' header; compare it with the secret shown in the 'Secret' section.
If the secret is compromised, use the recycle button (orange icon) to regenerate it without needing to create a new endpoint.

settingsLocalization.title: What do you configure in Localization?
settingsLocalization.description: Localization sets the timezone, currency, date/time format, and working language for your workspace. These settings affect how data is displayed in the dashboard and reports.
tips: Select the timezone where your team operates (e.g. 'Colombia (GMT-5)') so appointment schedules and reports match your local reality.
Choose the date format your customers use (e.g. 'DD/MM/YYYY' for LatAm) and the time format (24h or 12h) to avoid confusion in appointment confirmations.
The 'Currency' field defines the symbol shown in quotes and sales reports; change it if you operate in multiple countries.
Set 'First day of the week' to Monday or Sunday according to your country's calendar so the calendar views in the appointments module display correctly.

settingsMacros.title: What are macros?
settingsMacros.description: Macros are predefined action sequences that an agent can run with one click in the inbox. They automate repetitive tasks like assigning conversations, changing statuses, or adding tags.
tips: Create a 'Team' visibility macro so all agents can use common actions, for example: 'Escalate to supervisor' (action: change status to 'Waiting for agent').
Combine multiple actions in a single macro: first 'Assign agent', then 'Add tag' (e.g. 'vip'), and finally 'Change status' to 'Active'.
Macros with 'Personal' visibility are yours only; use them for personal workflows, such as adding an internal note with your follow-up template.
Use the 'Description' field to clarify when to apply each macro (e.g. 'Use when the customer asks for pricing a second time').

settingsMedia.title: What is the media bank for?
settingsMedia.description: The media bank is your centralized image gallery for use in campaigns, WhatsApp templates, and conversations. Upload, organize, and copy image URLs to reuse them across any module.
tips: Classify each image with the 'Type' selector ('General', 'Product', 'Course') before uploading so you can filter them easily from the gallery.
Add descriptive tags (e.g. 'promo-june', 'web-banner') to each image using the 'Edit' button; then filter by tag using the colored pills in the gallery.
Use 'Copy URL' (copy icon on the card) to paste the direct image link into a WhatsApp template or the campaign builder.
Drag and drop images directly onto the dotted area to upload them faster, without needing to click the upload zone.

settingsNotifications.title: How to configure your notifications?
settingsNotifications.description: Here you control which alerts you receive and through which channel. Adjust categories so you only get what truly matters and never miss key signals from your conversations.
tips: Enable 'Push notifications' to receive real-time alerts even when the dashboard is in the background.
If you get too many emails, change 'Email digest' to 'Daily' for one consolidated digest instead of one per event.
Disable the 'Automations' category if your flows are already stable and you don't need to monitor every trigger.
Always keep the 'Handoff' category active so you never miss a conversation transferred to a human agent.

settingsNurturing.title: How does automatic lead nurturing work?
settingsNurturing.description: Nurturing sequences automatically resend messages to leads who stopped replying. Configure timings, channels, and the final action to recover opportunities without manual intervention.
tips: Enable the 'Enable nurturing' toggle only when you have at least one channel selected; otherwise the sequence won't send any messages.
For WhatsApp, type in 'Template name' the exact Meta-approved name (e.g. 'reengagement_v2') — lowercase, no quotes.
Set 'Attempt 1' to 4 h and 'Attempt 2' to 24 h: that rhythm is less intrusive and reduces contact blocks.
Choose 'Create task' as the final action so the CRM generates a manual follow-up task when automatic attempts are exhausted.

settingsPipeline.title: How to customize pipeline stages?
settingsPipeline.description: Here you define your business sales funnel: names, colors, close probability, and transition rules per stage. A well-configured pipeline improves reporting and your team's workflow.
tips: Drag the 6-dot icon (⠿) to reorder stages without losing leads already in them.
Click the color picker on each row to assign a unique color; use green for closing stages (e.g. 'Won') and gray for negative terminals (e.g. 'Lost').
Set 'Probability' between 0 and 100 based on real historical close rates for that stage; this feeds the CRM forecast.
Use the 'Load industry presets' button to import pre-designed stages for your tenant's vertical, then customize them.

settingsPlatform.title: What do you configure in Platform settings?
settingsPlatform.description: This section is exclusive to super administrators and controls global engine parameters: platform name, default language and timezone, conversation limits, and module activation such as Analytics and RAG.
tips: Change the 'Platform name' to match your brand for white-label deployments (e.g. 'SalesBot Pro' instead of 'Parallext Engine').
Set the 'Default timezone' to the country where most of your tenants operate; this affects reports and send schedules.
Temporarily disable 'RAG enabled' during knowledge base migrations to avoid inconsistent responses.
The 'Analytics enabled' toggle controls platform-wide event tracking; keep it active to avoid losing conversion data.

settingsPlatformChangelog.title: How to publish updates to all tenants?
settingsPlatformChangelog.description: The changelog compiler lets you write, translate, and publish update announcements that appear in all tenants' dashboards as a 'What's new' modal. Manage history and edit previous entries from the 'History' tab.
tips: Fill in the title in Spanish first (required field), then switch language tabs (es/en/pt/fr) to translate before publishing.
Use the 'Add Section' button to add individual features; choose the right category: 'New' (blue), 'Improved' (green), or 'Fixed' (yellow).
Upload a screenshot per feature with 'Upload Screenshot/Image' to make the modal more visual and easier for end users to understand.
Leave 'Published' unchecked if you want to save a draft and review it in the live preview before tenants see it.

settingsPolicies.title: What are policies used for?
settingsPolicies.description: Store your business legal texts here (returns, warranty, privacy, etc.). Every time you save, a new numbered version is created so you have a full history.
tips: Use the left panel to switch types: 'Shipping', 'Return', 'Privacy', etc. The green badge shows the active version number.
The 'Title' field is the document's visible name; 'Content' accepts Markdown, so you can use **bold**, lists, and headings.
Click 'View history (v3)' to review previous versions of the same policy type without losing the current one.
Always save before switching policy types to avoid losing changes; the button reads 'Save new version' when a policy already exists.

settingsPrechat.title: How does the pre-chat form work?
settingsPrechat.description: The pre-chat form collects visitor data before the agent attends them. You can add fields like name, email, phone, or dropdowns, and the WhatsApp preview shows how it will look.
tips: Turn on the 'Active form' toggle so the form appears at the start of the conversation; disable it if you prefer to collect data only through the agent.
When adding a field, choose 'Map to' → 'contact.name' or 'contact.email' so data is saved directly to the contact profile.
